episodes.215801: During the 26th late afternoon and evening, a moist and unstable air mass interacted with an approaching upper-level disturbance and surface cold front across central and southern Indiana. Warm surface temperatures and high dew points fueled moderate instability, allowing scattered convective cells to initiate and rapidly intensify into strong to severe thunderstorms.||The severe weather event began in Howard County around 16:33 EST, where a severe thunderstorm produced 1.00-inch diameter hail near Russiaville. As the convective activity propagated south-southeastward through the evening, storms transitioned primarily into strong wind producers. Thunderstorm wind gusts estimated between 58 mph and 65 mph (50 to 56 knots) impacted multiple counties, including Morgan, Brown, Monroe, Lawrence, Jackson, Knox, and Martin between 18:41 EST and 21:35 EST. Peak estimated wind gusts reached up to 56 knots in Jackson and Martin counties.||The primary severe impact was scattered wind damage to trees. Thunderstorm wind gusts downed numerous trees, large tree limbs, and a few power lines. In Morgan County, fallen trees blocked a roadway and struck a utility pole, initiating a localized fire. Tree damage was widespread across Jackson and Martin counties which caused temporary road blockages and localized power outages throughout the affected areas.
episodes.215897: Scattered shower and thunderstorms began to form ahead of a cold frontal passage in an environment that experienced ample destabilization during the late morning and afternoon hours across eastern Pennsylvania. Thunderstorm coverage initially struggled to form across western Pennsylvania due to lack of shear; however, more organized thunderstorm activity began to occur east of the Allegheny Front. Thunderstorms were initially very slow moving and would often begin training, allowing for multiple instances of flash flooding during the evening hours. Flash flooding was most notable in the Harrisburg and Lancaster metro areas; however, flooding, including a water rescue due to cars being stranded in high water was also observed near Bloomsburg. Isolated instances of tree damage were also observed across southeastern Pennsylvania, with multiple instances of tree damage in Lebanon County.
episodes.215899: A pre-frontal trough ignited several discrete thunderstorms that coalesced into short line segments from mid afternoon through early evening. Although severe storms were rather widely spaced, storms that did turn severe produced numerous instances of wind damage and several instances of large hail.

episodes.215904: Storms trained over the same area near Martinsburg for approximately two hours in the early evening of August 27th. This resulted in localized rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches. Widespread flash flooding impacted the greater Martinsburg area, with impacts lasting through the evening.
episodes.216251: A surface cold front positioned northwest of West Virginia on the afternoon of August 27th gradually slid southeastward towards the area. Daytime heating and orographic lifting contributed to storm development that afternoon, resulting in tree and power line damage in Wyoming County. The threat for strong storms diminished quickly once the front dashed to the south and east.

episodes.216583: A weak frontal boundary moved across VT and northern NY during the afternoon and evening of August 27th and developed scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. One thunderstorm produced isolated wind damage in Westmore, VT.
episodes.216594: A stalled frontal boundary across the Piedmont of central North Carolina led to the development of late afternoon and evening thunderstorms across the eastern Piedmont, Sandhills, and southern Coastal Plain. Storms weakened in intensity by the mid-evening hours, but continued to produce heavy rainfall, leading to isolated flash flood reports across Scotland County.

episodes.216936: Strong to severe thunderstorms track east to southeast across the Denver area during the late afternoon and early evening hours of August 26th. Heavy rain and hail accompanied the stronger storms with hail up to 1.25 inch in diameter being reported.
episodes.217244: A pre-frontal trough moved through the region during the afternoon and evening, triggering thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front. Despite limited instability, strong wind shear supported organized storms with damaging wind gusts as the primary hazard.
episodes.217471: Isolated thunderstorms, relatively low-topped, along an advancing cold front were able to create a few instances of wind damage during the afternoon of August 27th.
episodes.217583: Isolated flash flooding occurred on 8/27 associated with a favorable environment where precipitable values were around 2 inches within a moist and unstable air mass with MLCAPE values over 2000 J/kg. Generally weak southwesterly flow ahead of an approaching upper trough allowed for training of convection with high rain rates.
episodes.217644: Dissipating convection and resultant outflow produced a severe wind gust near Frederick, OK on the morning of the 27th.
episodes.217735: A broad sub-tropical upper level ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over New Mexico resulted in a split flow northerly flow regime in the upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a quasi-stationary mid-level trough axis extended south-southeastward from the Mississippi Pine Belt region toward coastal Mississippi.  A meso-scale convective complex with embedded strong to severe thunderstorms developed over northwest Louisiana and then swept to the southeast into metro Baton Rouge during the overnight hours.  The severe storms within the mesoscale convective complex produced damaging wind gusts that resulted in a fatality in Pointe Coupee Parish.
episodes.217736: A broad sub-tropical upper level ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over New Mexico resulted in a split flow northerly flow regime in the upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a quasi-stationary mid-level trough axis extended south-southeastward from the Mississippi Pine Belt region toward coastal Mississippi. A meso-scale convective complex with embedded strong to severe thunderstorms developed over coastal Mississippi during the overnight hours. The severe storms within the mesoscale convective complex produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.217737: A broad sub-tropical upper level ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over New Mexico resulted in a split flow northerly flow regime in the upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a quasi-stationary mid-level trough axis extended south-southeastward from the Mississippi Pine Belt region toward coastal Mississippi. Two different meso-scale convective complexes with embedded strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the overnight hours.  The first mesoscale convective complex developed over coastal Mississippi and then pushed southward impacting the coastal waters off shore of Mississippi with severe marine thunderstorm wind gusts.  A second mesoscale convective complex also formed over northwest Louisiana and then quickly swept to the southeast impacting Lake Pontchartrain and the waters off the coast of Louisiana later in the night.  The severe storms within the mesoscale convective complex produced additional severe marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.217751: After a warm front lifted north of the area early in the day, enough clearing occurred to allow for showers and isolated thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon and evening well ahead of an approaching cold front. Rainfall was locally heavy which led to several streets flooding and water getting into a few basements.
episodes.217859: Isolated thunderstorms produced a high wind gust at the Junction airport and wind damage at San Angelo.
episodes.217884: Two days worth (27th and 28th) of southwesterly flow aloft was capped with an upper level low traversing the region on the 29th with a cold front. While none of the three days were particularly impressive from a setup perspective (Lacking one or more of forcing, thermodynamics, or kinematics), that did not stop the thunderstorms that formed from producing isolated severe reports.
episodes.217904: A weak frontal boundary moved into Central Texas generating showers and thunderstorms. Additional storms developed over South-Central Texas in a hot airmass. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.217973: A thunderstorm complex in central Nebraska moved south through southwestern Nebraska, and eventually into northwest Kansas, producing up to 1 inch hail and up to 60 mph wind gusts.
episodes.218213: A warm and moist airmass residing across the area supported thunderstorms capable of producing strong wind gusts while shifting across coastal waters.
episodes.218214: Deep moisture, weak shear and ample instability supported slow moving showers and   thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall and flash flooding, especially across parts of Beaufort and Hampton Counties in the Yemassee area. A COOP Observer located in Yemassee reported a 24-hour rainfall amount of 10 inches, most of which occurred between 2 PM to 830 PM.
episodes.218320: During the evening hours on August 26th, a mid-level trough and associated surface cold front descended into the Ohio Valley from the north and west. The better shear and instability had been present to the north of the region earlier in the evening; however, there was still around 1000 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE and around 25 knots of effective bulk shear as a cluster of storms along the front moved into southern Indiana during the late evening hours. Ultimately, these storms only produced one instance of wind damage, and storms dissipated as they reached the Ohio River.
episodes.218325: A warm front passed through the region in the morning hours of Thursday, August 27th, 2026, placing eastern New York within the warm sector of a surface cyclone translating eastward from southeast Ontario into southwest Quebec. A surface trough propagating through the warm sector ahead of the main cold front forced the development of scattered thunderstorms, some of which became severe, that afternoon and evening. The most notable storms occurred in the Upper-Hudson Valley, specifically in Saratoga County, where two weak tornadoes eventually formed. The first, an EF-1 in Wilton, snapped and uprooted numerous softwood and hardwood trees during its 4 minute, 1.22 mile track. The second, an EF-0, uprooted several softwood trees near Ruggles Road and Preserve Way. The storm which spawned the tornadoes caused a fair amount of wind damage itself, mainly in the town of Wilton but outside of the 250 yard tornado width. ||A few other severe storms developed in Ulster and Herkimer Counties, leading to additional tree and wire damage near Shandaken, Napanoch, and Cold Brook. A third weak tornado also developed in southwest Hamilton County as the aforementioned severe storm in Herkimer crossed into its border. This was another very brief EF-0 which caused numerous softwood trees to snap and become uprooted in a remote area of the Adirondacks.
episodes.218480: With the subtropical ridge remaining in place, a stronger trough would impact the Pacific Northwest resulting in more widespread flash flooding across southern and central Utah, as well as widespread severe weather across the majority of Utah. This would go on to produce a prolific wind-driven hail event in Lynndyl, Utah.
episodes.218482: A subtropical high would begin to establish itself over the central U.S. before sliding east somewhat with modest troughing off the western U.S. coastline. This would set the stage for isolated severe weather across the Dugway area.
episodes.218534: An early morning complex of thunderstorms tracked out of eastern Colorado and into western Kansas. A lone severe wind gust was measured in Kearny County.
episodes.218564: Southerly flow over the peninsula supports early afternoon convection that produces strong marine wind gusts from Tampa Bay southward to coastal Lee County waters near Punta Rassa.
